sections.h2: Where does a Columbia County, GA homeowner deal with property tax?
sections.html:
Property tax in Columbia County is handled at the Tax Commissioner's Property Tax Division in Evans, 630 Ronald Reagan Drive, Building C, Second Floor, Evans, GA 30809. Call 706-261-8299 for property tax. Doors open at 8 am and close at 4:30 pm on non-holiday weekdays.

The same division takes homestead applications, runs the delinquent tax unit, and posts the county digest and a tax worksheet. Valuation sits with a separate assessment office, so a question about why your house is worth what the notice says is not a tax commissioner question. Ask the division for the right contact if you are unsure where to start.

  • Bills, payments and payoffs: Tax Commissioner, Property Tax Division.
  • Homestead applications: same office in Evans.
  • Delinquent accounts and sheriff's tax sales: Delinquent Tax Division.
  • Mobile home permits: Planning and Zoning in Evans, or city hall in Grovetown or Harlem.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Columbia County for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Columbia County is a fast-growing suburban county on the Savannah River, part of the Augusta metropolitan area. Wikipedia gives its area as 308 square miles and lists Grovetown and Harlem as its cities, with Appling, Evans and Martinez as census-designated places. Appling is the legal county seat, while Evans is where county government actually operates.

Interstate 20 crosses the county, and US 78 and US 221 are among the other major roads. Clarks Hill Lake, also called Strom Thurmond Lake, is among the county's named waters. The Columbia County School District covers the whole county. Growth is the story here: the 2020 census counted 156,010 residents, and the latest July 2025 estimate of 169,189 is 8.4% higher.

QuickFacts lists 65,264 housing units. Owners hold 78.1% of them, the typical owned home is valued at $305,300, rent averages $1,409 and household income is $95,592. Those figures describe the county as a whole, not any one street.

sections.h2: How is a Columbia County tax bill built?
sections.html:
The county's tax worksheet page lays out the steps: fair market value times 40% gives the assessed value, and assessed value times the millage rate gives the tax. The millage rate is expressed in dollars for every thousand of assessed value, and it comes from the proposed budget divided by the tax digest, which is the total of all assessments.

Exemptions come off before the rate is applied. The county posts a downloadable tax calculation workbook labeled for estimating only, and it warns that a change in rates, values or fees changes the final amount. Use it to compare scenarios, then get the official figure from the division.

Payment can be made online through the county's pay-tax page. Credit cards carry a third-party processing fee, and an eCheck carries a $1.50 per item fee. If your lender escrows the tax, the county asks you to contact the lender first so nothing is paid twice.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions does Columbia County offer?
sections.html:
The county lists a regular exemption plus several age, disability and veteran exemptions, and each reduces the assessed value rather than the market value. Applications are taken at the Evans office, and the county says you must apply no later than April 1 to get the benefit for the same year. The office accepts applications year-round.

  • Regular homestead (S1): up to $10,000 off assessed value, for state, county and school purposes, excluding bond taxes and city taxes.
  • Age 62 (L3): $40,000 off for county and school, with net income of both spouses not over $15,000.
  • Local school exemption, age 70 (L6): the school tax on the home and up to three adjoining acres, no income limit.
  • Disabled veteran (S5): $126,526 off, with a VA letter showing 100% service-connected, total and permanent disability, refreshed every three years.
  • Total and permanent disability (L5): $40,000 off, with two physician affidavits and the same $15,000 income cap.
  • Surviving spouse of a military member (SS): $126,526 off, and a full exemption for the spouse of a firefighter or peace officer killed in the line of duty.

Bring a Georgia driver's license showing your current address, the vehicle registration card showing Columbia County, a recorded deed, and income returns where the exemption has an income test. Any change to the deed, a refinance for example, requires a new application.

sections.h2: What does the January 1 rule mean if I sell my Columbia County house?
sections.html:
Georgia assigns a year's tax to whoever owned the property on January 1, and the county's tax office does not split the bill between buyer and seller. That split is a closing matter. The Columbus tax commissioner's explanation of the same state rule says a lien stays in the January 1 owner's name unless proof within 90 days of the due date shows the buyer contractually took the tax.

For you, that means two practical steps. First, read the proration line on the settlement statement and confirm the title company will pay the county, not leave it for the buyer to find. Second, if a Columbia County bill is still unpaid at closing, ask the Property Tax Division for the exact payoff for the closing date. The division mails each bill to the owner named in its records, so a seller who has moved should confirm the address on file.

The county's pay-tax page lets you view the tax on a parcel online, which helps you spot a balance before a buyer's title search does.

sections.h2: How are delinquent Columbia County taxes enforced?
sections.html:
The county first tries a letter or phone call, and if that fails it uses a levy and a sheriff's tax sale. The delinquent tax page says most matters are settled without a sale, and that the county has one of the highest collection rates in Georgia.

Sheriff's tax sales are public auctions that open at the amount of tax owed, and they are held on the first Tuesday of the month when the office schedules one. The sale notice appears in the Augusta Chronicle legal ads about a month ahead, as well as on the county site.

An owner who is behind should talk to the division before the levy stage. Selling the house before a sale date is possible, because the payoff is settled from the proceeds at the closing table, but the numbers must be confirmed in writing first.

sections.html:

The county does not print a due date on the pages above, so read the date on your bill or ask the division. Georgia's usual window to contest a value is 45 days from the date of the assessment notice, and the notice itself states the deadline for your parcel.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for a Columbia County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: At the Tax Commissioner's Property Tax Division in Evans, 630 Ronald Reagan Drive, Building C, Second Floor. Applications are accepted year-round, but the county says the benefit for the current year requires filing by April 1.

faqs.q: Do I need to reapply after refinancing?
faqs.a: Yes. The county states that any change to a deed, a refinance for example, requires a new homestead application.

faqs.q: Is there a Columbia County exemption with no income limit?
faqs.a: Yes. The local school exemption for homeowners 70 or older covers the school tax on the house and up to three contiguous acres, and the county describes it as having no income limit.

faqs.q: How often are Columbia County tax sales held?
faqs.a: On the first Tuesday of the month, when the office schedules one. They are sheriff's tax sales run as auctions, and the notice is published in the Augusta Chronicle about a month earlier.

faqs.q: Can I pay Columbia County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the county's pay-tax page. A credit card carries a third-party fee, an eCheck carries $1.50 per item, and the county asks escrow customers to check with their lender first.
